previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and GERD was admitted for chest pressure, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal EKGs and negative troponins. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction but supported constipation as a contributor. Symptoms improved after a GI cocktail and bowel movements with laxatives. Her chest pain was attributed to GERD, and she was started on ranitidine. Acute kidney injury, likely prerenal from dehydration, improved with IV fluids. Her home medications were continued, with instructions to restart lisinopril and HCTZ. She expressed concern about unsafe housing due to cockroach infestation, prompting social work consultation. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for a stress test and medication management.

the day prior to these pains. She also reports stomach pains and 
diarrhea 1 day ago. She also endorses some palpitations. She 
also complained of dysuria and urinary frequency for the past 
few days.

On arrival to the ED, her VS were 97.8 67 198/78 20 99%2L. Her 
BP settled to the 160's systolic soon after arrival. She was 
given SL NTG as well as morphine 4 mg IV without complete 
resolution of her pain. Her troponin returned at 0.28; EKG 
reportedly was consistent with priors. Given her elevated 
troponin and continued pain, she started on a heparin gtt as 
well as a NTG gtt. Rectal exam was performed and was guaiac 
negative. She was also given ASA 325 mg and plavix loaded. Labs 
in the ED were also significant for a glucose of 446. There was 
no anion gap on chem 7 and no ketones on UA. Per report, she had 
taken 50 units of Lantus this evening. In the ED, she was given 
2L IVFs as well as 10 units of humalog. Repeat ___ after fluids 
(but prior to humalog) was ~400. Given her ""kidney"" pain, UA was 
performed and was negative for infection. CXR showed ?RLL 
opacification and mild pulmonary edema per preliminary read. VS 
prior to transfer to the floor were 137/60 55 21 97%2L.  
.  
On arrival to the floor, the patient's VS were BP=137/55 HR=63 
RR=20 O2 sat=96%2L. She reported that her chest pain had 
completely resolved. She did report some mild lingering 
bilateral flank pain. She denied and lightheadedness, shortness 
of breath, nausea, diaphoresis. She did admit to some chronic 
dizziness and gait instability.  
.  
.  
On review of systems, she denies any prior history of stroke, 
TIA, deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, bleeding at the 
time of surgery, myalgias, joint pains, cough, hemoptysis, black 
stools or red stools. She denies recent fevers, chills or 
rigors. All of the other review of systems were negative.  
.  
Cardiac review of systems is notable for absence of ankle edema, 
syncope or presyncope. She does report some chronic SOB but does 
not endorse any current SOB.  
.

Brief Hospital Course:

found to have elevated troponins on labs.

# CORONARIES: Mrs. ___ has known CAD with prior PCI and is 
s/p CABG w/LIMA-LAD, SVG-OM, SVG-RPDA in ___. She was 
admitted with NSTEMI per symptoms and positive troponin to 0.28. 
Her EKG was minimally changed from baseline mainly showing 
mildly progressed ST depression and deeper TWI in V4. While 
demand ischemia d/t high BPs (198/70 in the ED) at presentation 
was initially considered in the differential diagnosis of her 
positive cardiac enzymes the patient's symptoms, EKG changes and 
rich coronary history warranted management as per NSTEMI. She 
was treated with Aspirin, BB, ACE-I, high dose Statin, IV 
Heparin and Plavix was loaded. Her pain resolved with IV 
Morphine and NG ___. Her high TIMI risk score indicated pursuit 
of an early catheterization strategy which on ___ demonstrated 
multiple coronary lesions (see report above). She had successful 
PCI to SVG to RCA with 2 bare metal stents in the mid portion of 
the graft. She was completely pain free after the procedure and 
the rest of her course was uncomplicated. She is discharged with 
Aspirin 325mg daily and Plavix 75mg for a minimum of 3 months. 
Of note on this admission Metoprolol Succinate was increased 
from 50 to 100mg daily, Lisinopril was increased from 20mg to 
40mg daily and Simvastatin was increased from 40mg to 80mg 
daily.
.

diuresis. She was completely symptom-free on discharge and was 
able to ambulate comfortably without desaturation. Repeat 
echocardiography may be considered in the outpatient setting. 
.

Treatment with Lantus + ISS was continued. Referral to diabetic

# Asthma: This was stable and Mrs. ___ had no respiratory
